About.title: About Field Signal
About.intro: Field Signal brings together 25 years of data on weather, soil moisture and plant health, so you can see how different rotations would have done on your field.
About.judgment: The tool supports the farmer's judgment. It does not replace it.

what.farmer: For farmers: compares your current rotation with two alternatives (at least one with peas) and shows, year by year, how each would have done.
what.buyer: For feed buyers: shows, by commune, the risk of not finding enough harvest, quality risks (aflatoxins, fusarium, harvest rain) and environmental impact.
what.transparency: Every number shows its source, period, assumptions and confidence next to it.

About.sourcesHint: Public data. Resolution shows how big each source's “pixel” is.

sources.power: Heat, rain and air humidity, day by day
sources.modis: How green and vigorous the vegetation is (NDVI)
sources.smap: Water in the soil, around the roots
sources.soilgrids: Organic carbon, pH and soil texture
sources.eucropmap: Which crops grow where, for areas per commune
sources.ins: Official county yields, to check the model

ai.model: A small model estimates the chance of a poor year for each zone and crop, from weather and vegetation signals in the critical periods. We test it by leaving out one year at a time and publish both hits and misses.
ai.text: A language model turns the computed numbers into plain text. It may only use values we computed, in a fixed format.

limits.hail: Hail and other short, local weather events.
limits.pests: Pests and diseases in your field.
limits.management: Your field work, hybrids and fertiliser.
limits.scale: Weather data describe an area tens of kilometres wide, not your exact plot.

About.demo: In this version the numbers are for demonstration. We mark them clearly as “Demo data” until the real data are connected.
About.judgmentDetail: It shows what would have happened in past years. The decision for your field stays yours.
About.nasaNote: We use free public data published by NASA and other institutions. NASA is not a partner and does not endorse this tool.
About.aiHint: AI does two small, checkable jobs. It does not make decisions for you.

Stocks.title: Stocks and suppliers
Stocks.intro: How many days the ingredients in stock will last, and which countries can make up the gap to 90 days.
Stocks.demo: Demo data — illustrative scenario. Stocks and supplier volumes are invented; trade rules are public, and lead times are estimates.
Stocks.context: As of {date} · marketing year {year} · sourcing window {window}
Stocks.inventoryHint: Tap an ingredient to see its suppliers.
Stocks.inventoryCaption: Stocks, use and days of cover, most exposed ingredient first
Stocks.legend: Critical: under {red} days. Watch: under {amber} days. Covered: {amber} days or more. Target: {target} days of cover.
Stocks.noShortfall: Stock already covers {target} days. Nothing needs buying now.
Stocks.noCandidates: We have no supplier forecasts for this ingredient.
Stocks.allocationHint: Conservative: we use each country's lowest volume estimate and at most 4 countries.
Stocks.uncovered: {tonnes} stay uncovered by the forecast suppliers. Look for an alternative ingredient or a new supplier.
Stocks.bridge: Some recommended deliveries arrive after the stock runs out: a bridge purchase from a nearby supplier is needed.
Stocks.concentrated: Over half of the volume comes from one country: concentration risk.
Stocks.alternatives: Alternatives in the same group with enough stock: {list}.
Stocks.volumeLabel: Estimated volume between {low} and {high} t, central value {mid} t
Stocks.history: Volume in marketing years {first}–{last} (dashed line: mean)

method.cover: Days of cover = (stock + incoming) ÷ daily use, where daily use = monthly use ÷ 30. Under {red} days is critical; under {amber} days needs watching.
method.shortfall: Shortfall = the tonnes missing to reach {target} days of cover.
method.score: A country's score (0–100) = {coverage}% coverage + {reliability}% reliability + {logistics}% logistics + {friction}% ease of trade.
method.coverage: Coverage: how much of the shortfall the country's central volume estimate covers on its own.
method.reliability: Reliability: half the forecast confidence, half how narrow the volume range is.
method.logistics: Logistics: 100 points at 2 days' lead time, falling linearly to 0 at 50 days.
method.friction: Ease of trade: starts at 100. We subtract 30 outside the EU, 30 for war risk, 10 for 1520 mm rail gauge, 15 for 2022 export curbs, and 20 for soy meal from countries where GM soy is common.
method.allocation: Split: we take at most 4 countries, in score order. In the first pass each gives at most its lowest volume estimate and at most half the shortfall; the second pass tops each up to its lowest estimate, uncapped.
method.assumptions: Assumptions: stocks, use and supplier volumes are invented. EU and Schengen rules, rail gauge and the 2022 export curbs are public facts. Lead times are estimates. Prices are not part of the calculation.
